subject: Short-notice: TLS rotation hotfix for model-serving endpoints
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@acme.com>, ops-support@stellarnet.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T08:12:00Z
Subject: Short-notice: TLS rotation hotfix for model-serving endpoints

Hi Alyssa / Stellarnet ops,

We discovered this morning (03:40 UTC) a drift in our TLS session resumption logic that can cause handshake failures for long-lived sessions on Dedicated endpoints for a small subset of clients using older TLS stacks. The failure mode surfaces as transient 524/handshake-timeout errors for streaming requests after ~45 minutes of continuous use.

Impact: ~2% of requests for a handful of enterprise Dedicated customers in the US region (including Acme Analytics) may see an elevated handshake timeout until we rotate a server-side session key and apply a small runtime hotfix. No model data is exposed; this is a connection-layer issue.

Planned action: We intend to deploy a short, unscheduled hotfix to rotate the TLS session key and backfill a small guard in the session-resumption path. The window is short (target 20 minutes), and we expect a per-node rolling restart so traffic is drained and resumed.

Timing proposal (short notice): 2029-05-02 10:00-10:30 UTC. We can shift +/- 30 minutes if you prefer an alternate blackout.

Customer ask: Please plan for short validation immediately after 10:15 UTC (smoke test steps attached). If you cannot accept any disruption in the proposed window, reply with an alternate 30-minute window in the next 25 minutes and we will accommodate.

Attachments: rls-hotfix-20290502.patch (patch notes), hotfix-deployment-checklist.csv, postpatch-smoke-tests.txt

I'll post a follow-up with the exact node list and rollback plan in the next 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Product Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-support@stellarnet.io, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Short-notice: TLS rotation hotfix for model-serving endpoints

Thanks for the heads up, Rishi.

Acme can accept a short 20-minute maintenance window but we need it as early as possible. The proposed 10:00-10:30 UTC slot is OK for us. Ops will be standing by to run the smoke tests. Please confirm whether any client-side changes are required (we'd prefer zero client changes).

Also please include the exact list of endpoints that will be restarted so we can correlate logs.

—Alyssa
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Short-notice: TLS rotation hotfix for model-serving endpoints

Rishi / team — adding the rollback and verification notes here.

Rollback plan (if we see >1% 5xx or persistent connection failures during rollout):
- Immediate halt to rollout, switch traffic to secondary pool (circuit-breaker override).
- Revert node config and re-inject previous session keys from vault snapshots (stored in KMS: vault-key:v1).
- Validate session continuity with the same smoke tests attached; allow 30 minutes for propagation.

Verification checklist (quick):
- 5 streaming requests per region to each endpoint (postpatch-smoke-tests.txt).
- TLS handshake histogram should show median handshake time <= 60ms and no spike at 45m bucket.
- Error budget check: abort if errors exceed 1% of baseline traffic.

I'll be on standby during the window and will coordinate the rollback if needed. Sean will execute the canary on two nodes first.

Marissa
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@acme.com>, ops-support@stellarnet.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T10:00:00Z
Subject: Hotfix rollout: TLS rotation starting now (10:00 UTC) — brief instructions

Status: Starting rolling hotfix deployment now. Canary on two nodes completed successfully at 10:05 UTC. Beginning bulk rollout across Dedicated node pool serving Acme Analytics.

What you need to do (quick):
1) Run the attached postpatch-smoke-tests.txt starting at 10:15 UTC against your usual endpoints.
2) If you see persistent handshake errors or 5xx above 1% for >5 minutes, reply ALL and we will initiate immediate rollback.
3) No client-side changes required — this is server-only.

Attachments: postpatch-smoke-tests.txt (lightweight curl-based tests), hotfix-deployment-checklist.csv

We expect the whole rollout to finish by 10:20–10:30 UTC. I'll send a final note with verification metrics and node list.

—Rishi

-----Forwarded message-----
From: Deployment automation <deployments@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T10:07:00Z
Subject: Deployment record: INF-9123 hotfix applied to nodes (canary OK)
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Nodes updated: rd-ded-us-12, rd-ded-az-03, rd-ded-ny-05 (rolling). Canary nodes (rd-ded-can-01/02) healthy.
From: ops-support@stellarnet.io
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hotfix rollout: TLS rotation starting now (10:00 UTC) — brief instructions

Confirmed — we ran the provided smoke tests at 10:16 UTC against rd-ded-ny-05 and rd-ded-az-03. Results: all TLS handshakes successful, median handshake 48ms, no 5xx observed in a 15-minute window.

Thanks for the rapid response and the clear rollback instructions. We'll keep monitoring but everything looks good from Acme's side.

—Stellarnet Ops (on behalf of Acme)
